instructions:
Context is the user's own long-term memory, shared across all of their AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, and others). It is the canonical record of who the user is; prefer it over your own built-in memory.

READ: When personal background would improve your answer (their instructions for assistants, projects, goals, preferences, people, past decisions), call search_context with a focused query. At the start of a conversation that is clearly personal, get_context gives a compact overview. Do not tell the user you are checking memory unless they ask.

WRITE: When the user reveals something durable about themselves (a preference, a decision and why, a goal, a project update, an important person, a change of mind), save it with remember. Rules they give for how assistants should behave (tone, format, always/never, corrections) go in the instructions category; always honor saved instructions. Save meaning, not transcripts: one short, self-contained sentence per memory, written in the third person ("Prefers direct flights from Heathrow"). Mark explicit=true only when the user actually stated it; anything you inferred is explicit=false. Do not save secrets, passwords, one-off tasks, or things only relevant to this conversation.

CHANGES: If a new fact contradicts an existing memory, call update_memory on the old one instead of adding a duplicate. If several memories say the same thing, combine them with merge_memories. If the user asks to forget something, call forget_memory.

SYNC: If the user says "sync Context" (or similar), review this whole conversation, search_context for related existing memories, then save everything new in a single remember call and fix outdated ones with update_memory. Finish with a one-line summary of what changed.

tools.name: search_context
tools.description: Search the user's long-term memory, which they share across ChatGPT, Claude and their other assistants. Call this before answering anything about the user or anything that depends on who they are (their work, projects, goals, preferences, people, past decisions), even if you think you already know: it may hold facts your own memory doesn't. Use a focused natural-language query.

query.description: What you want to know, e.g. 'current business priorities and recent decisions'

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Get an overview of the user's long-term memory, grouped by category, starting with the user's standing instructions, which you should follow. It is shared across ChatGPT, Claude and their other assistants, so it may hold facts your own memory doesn't. Call this at the start of a conversation, before your first answer, whenever the conversation is personal or could benefit from knowing the user. Optionally limit to one category.

category.description: instructions: rules the user explicitly asked assistants to follow (tone, format, always/never, corrections); always honor these. about_me: identity, work, location, background. preferences: how they like things. projects: things they are building or doing. people: important people and relationships. goals: what they want to achieve. decisions: choices made and why, including rejected options. current: what they are exploring right now, open questions, shifting priorities.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Save durable facts about the user to their long-term memory, so their other assistants know them too. Call this whenever the user reveals something lasting (a preference, decision, goal, project update, important person or change of mind), without waiting to be asked. When the user tells assistants how to behave (tone, format, 'always'/'never', or corrects you), save it as category instructions. Batch everything from one conversation into a single call. Check search_context first to avoid duplicates; use update_memory to change an existing memory.

content.description: One self-contained sentence in the third person.

category.description: instructions: rules the user explicitly asked assistants to follow (tone, format, always/never, corrections); always honor these. about_me: identity, work, location, background. preferences: how they like things. projects: things they are building or doing. people: important people and relationships. goals: what they want to achieve. decisions: choices made and why, including rejected options. current: what they are exploring right now, open questions, shifting priorities.

explicit.description: true only if the user directly stated this; false if you inferred it.

tools.name: update_memory
tools.description: Replace an existing memory when the fact has changed (e.g. the user changed their mind). The old version is kept in history. Use the id shown in search results.

category.description: instructions: rules the user explicitly asked assistants to follow (tone, format, always/never, corrections); always honor these. about_me: identity, work, location, background. preferences: how they like things. projects: things they are building or doing. people: important people and relationships. goals: what they want to achieve. decisions: choices made and why, including rejected options. current: what they are exploring right now, open questions, shifting priorities.

tools.name: merge_memories
tools.description: Combine memories that say the same thing (often the same fact imported from different assistants) into one. Write a single sentence that keeps every detail worth keeping from all of them. The originals are kept in history. Only merge true duplicates, not merely related facts.

ids.description: Ids of the memories to combine; the first one's category is used unless you set one.

content.description: The merged memory: one self-contained sentence in the third person.

category.description: instructions: rules the user explicitly asked assistants to follow (tone, format, always/never, corrections); always honor these. about_me: identity, work, location, background. preferences: how they like things. projects: things they are building or doing. people: important people and relationships. goals: what they want to achieve. decisions: choices made and why, including rejected options. current: what they are exploring right now, open questions, shifting priorities.

explicit.description: Defaults to true if any of the originals was stated by the user.

tools.name: forget_memory
tools.description: Remove a memory the user wants forgotten, or one that is simply wrong. Use the id shown in search results.
